Part 4. CPD data note and submission

CPD data note







Item
Description




Source
Compilation of Presidential Documents (CPD), accessed through GovInfo. The analytical corpus contained 352 documents: 183 associated with Biden and 169 with Trump. Administration labels were obtained from GovInfo’s dedicated president metadata.


Permission
Under GovInfo’s public-domain and copyright notice, official U.S. government works are generally available for public use. Government publications may also contain third-party copyrighted material, so availability does not establish unrestricted rights to every included item. The submission provides the collection log and metadata manifest rather than the downloaded documents.


Query
The search selected CPD documents matching the phrase "Xi Jinping", using a publication-date range beginning January 20, 2021. Query: collection:cpd "Xi Jinping" publishdate:range(2021-01-20,END_DATE). Replace END_DATE with the exact date recorded in cpd_collection_note.txt.


Collection date
Insert the actual collection date from the saved collection records. The rendered output does not display it.


Selection
The collection procedure was designed to retrieve all search-result pages and retain unique package IDs. PDFs were downloaded, text was extracted, and documents were grouped using president metadata. The rendered report confirms the analytical sample size but does not itself establish that every available matching document was successfully collected. Confirm completeness against the saved log before making that claim.


Gaps and limitations
The exact phrase may miss references using only “Xi,” other names, or alternative wording. Publication dates can differ from event dates. Extracted text includes editorial notes, names, headings, and question labels. The administrations have different periods of coverage and potentially different document compositions. The corpus captures published public communications rather than private diplomacy or public opinion.

title: Assignment 6: Summary and Interpretation
section: What we did overall in the code
text:
What we did overall in the code

Loaded the R packages needed to organize text, calculate statistics, fit models, and make plots.
Imported the archived summit tweets and checked missing and repeated text.
Converted text into tokens and document-feature matrices, making word use countable.
Calculated word frequencies to identify prominent terms in the tweet archive.
Constructed hashtag and mention networks to examine which labels and accounts appeared together.
Ran LSA to summarize tweet vocabulary patterns using four dimensions.
Searched GovInfo for CPD documents mentioning Xi Jinping, downloaded documents, and retained collection records.
Assigned administrations using official president metadata, rather than relying only on publication dates.
Used KWIC to read references to Xi within surrounding text.
Calculated administration keyness to identify relatively distinctive Biden and Trump vocabulary.
Selected inaugural addresses from 1945 onward and compared speech length, vocabulary diversity, and readability.
Calculated cosine similarity and party keyness to compare vocabulary across presidents and parties.
Confirmed that the 2025 inaugural address was included.
Estimated Wordfish positions and examined associated words, historical patterns, and party overlap.
Saved the corpus and model results and revised the rendering workflow so the report could reuse completed work instead of repeating collection and expensive calculations.
Rendered the analyses into a report containing plots, tables, and links to collection records.

63. 3a(i) — Reported versus received comments

## =============================================================================
## 3a(i) — Reported versus received comments
## =============================================================================

received_reported <- counts_all |>
  transmute(
    video_period,
    channel_title,
    video_id,
    status,
    comments_reported,
    comments_received = n_unique,
    reported_minus_received = comments_reported - n_unique,
    received_percent = if_else(
      comments_reported > 0,
      100 * n_unique / comments_reported,
      NA_real_
    ),
    reached_cap = n_unique >= 300,
    interpretation = case_when(

      n_unique > comments_reported ~

      n_unique >= 300 & comments_reported > n_unique ~
        "Collection reached the 300-comment cap",
      n_unique == comments_reported ~
        "Counts match at collection",
      TRUE ~
        "Difference remains unexplained by these records"
    )
  )

66. Distribution of likes and share held by the top 1%

## =============================================================================
## Distribution of likes and share held by the top 1%
## =============================================================================

summarise_likes <- function(x) {

  observed <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n_observed <- length(observed)

  if (n_observed == 0L) {
    return(tibble(
      comments_with_likes = 0L,
      missing_like_counts = length(x),
      zero_like_percent = NA_real_,
      mean_likes = NA_real_,
      median_likes = NA_real_,
      p90_likes = NA_real_,
      p99_likes = NA_real_,
      maximum_likes = NA_real_,
      total_likes = NA_real_,
      top_1pct_n = 0L,
      top_1pct_like_percent = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  top_n <- ceiling(0.01 * n_observed)
  total <- sum(observed)

  tibble(
    comments_with_likes = n_observed,
    missing_like_counts = sum(is.na(x)),
    zero_like_percent = 100 * mean(observed == 0),
    mean_likes = mean(observed),
    median_likes = median(observed),
    p90_likes = unname(quantile(observed, 0.90)),
    p99_likes = unname(quantile(observed, 0.99)),
    maximum_likes = max(observed),
    total_likes = total,
    top_1pct_n = top_n,
    top_1pct_like_percent = if (total > 0) {
      100 * sum(head(sort(observed, decreasing = TRUE), top_n)) / total
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

author_id_candidates <- c(
  "author_channel_id",
  "author_channel_id_value",
  "authorChannelId"
)

available_author_fields <- intersect(
  author_id_candidates,
  names(comments_all)
)

if (length(available_author_fields) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "Author ID column not found. Run names(comments_all) and share ",
    "the column names only; do not share author identities."
  )
}

author_id_field <- available_author_fields[1]

comments_all <- comments_all |>
  mutate(
    author_id_analysis = as.character(.data[[author_id_field]]),
    author_id_analysis = na_if(trimws(author_id_analysis), "")
  )

summarise_authors <- function(data) {

  identified <- data |>
    filter(!is.na(author_id_analysis))

  author_counts <- identified |>
    count(author_id_analysis, name = "n_comments") |>
    arrange(desc(n_comments), author_id_analysis)

  n_authors <- nrow(author_counts)
  top_n <- ceiling(0.10 * n_authors)
  top_comments <- sum(head(author_counts$n_comments, top_n))

  tibble(
    total_comments = nrow(data),
    comments_with_author_id = nrow(identified),
    comments_missing_author_id = nrow(data) - nrow(identified),
    unique_identifiable_authors = n_authors,
    top_10pct_authors_n = top_n,
    comments_from_top_authors = top_comments,
    top_author_share_identified_percent = if (nrow(identified) > 0) {
      100 * top_comments / nrow(identified)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },
    top_author_share_all_comments_percent = if (n_authors > 0) {
      100 * top_comments / nrow(data)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

68. Exact duplicate comment text

## =============================================================================
## Exact duplicate comment text
## =============================================================================

summarise_duplicates <- function(data) {

  eligible <- data |>
    filter(
      !is.na(text_original),
      nzchar(trimws(text_original))
    )

  text_counts <- eligible |>
    count(text_original, name = "n_copies")

  repeated <- text_counts |>
    filter(n_copies > 1)

  tibble(
    total_comments = nrow(data),
    comments_with_nonblank_text = nrow(eligible),
    missing_or_blank_text = nrow(data) - nrow(eligible),
    distinct_repeated_texts = nrow(repeated),
    comments_in_repeated_text_groups = sum(repeated$n_copies),
    duplicate_copies_beyond_first = sum(repeated$n_copies - 1L),
    duplicate_copies_percent = if (nrow(eligible) > 0) {
      100 * sum(repeated$n_copies - 1L) / nrow(eligible)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  )
}

94. Step 3b(v) — Lexicoder sentiment baseline

## =============================================================================
## Step 3b(v) — Lexicoder sentiment baseline
## =============================================================================

library(quanteda)

lsd_basic <- data_dictionary_LSD2015[
  c("positive", "negative")
]

dfm_sentiment_base <- dfm(toks_base)

dfm_sentiment_counts <- dfm_lookup(
  dfm_sentiment_base,
  dictionary = lsd_basic,
  valuetype = "glob",
  case_insensitive = TRUE
)

sentiment_counts <- as.data.frame(
  as.matrix(dfm_sentiment_counts)
) |>
  rownames_to_column("comment_id")

sentiment_metadata <- as_tibble(
  docvars(dfm_sentiment_base)
) |>
  mutate(
    comment_id = docnames(dfm_sentiment_base),
    .before = 1
  )

sentiment_results <- sentiment_metadata |>
  left_join(
    sentiment_counts,
    by = "comment_id",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    matched_terms = positive + negative,

    net_sentiment = if_else(
      matched_terms > 0,
      (positive - negative) / matched_terms,
      NA_real_
    ),

    dictionary_label = case_when(
      positive > negative ~ "positive",
      negative > positive ~ "negative",
      TRUE ~ "neither"
    ),

    no_dictionary_matches = matched_terms == 0
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(sentiment_results) == ndoc(corp_yt),
  !anyDuplicated(sentiment_results$comment_id)
)

98. 3b(v): Validate dictionary sentiment

## =============================================================================
## 3b(v): Validate dictionary sentiment
## =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(readr)

## Select the completed 40-comment CSV
validation_labels <- read_csv(
  file.choose(),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

sentiment_results <- readRDS(
  "data/youtube/text_analysis/sentiment_results.rds"
)

## Check labels and IDs before joining
valid_labels <- c("positive", "negative", "neither")

validation_labels <- validation_labels |>
  mutate(human_label = tolower(trimws(human_label)))

stopifnot(
  nrow(validation_labels) == 40,
  !anyDuplicated(validation_labels$comment_id),
  !anyDuplicated(sentiment_results$comment_id),
  all(validation_labels$human_label %in% valid_labels)
)

## Match reference labels to dictionary classifications
validation_comparison <- validation_labels |>
  select(validation_id, comment_id, human_label, text_original) |>
  left_join(
    sentiment_results |>
      select(comment_id, dictionary_label),
    by = "comment_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(agreement = human_label == dictionary_label)

stopifnot(
  all(validation_comparison$dictionary_label %in% valid_labels)
)

## Confusion matrix: rows = reference; columns = dictionary
confusion_matrix <- with(
  validation_comparison,
  table(
    reference = factor(human_label, levels = valid_labels),
    dictionary = factor(dictionary_label, levels = valid_labels)
  )
)

## Percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa
observed_agreement <- mean(validation_comparison$agreement)

expected_agreement <- sum(
  (rowSums(confusion_matrix) / sum(confusion_matrix)) *
    (colSums(confusion_matrix) / sum(confusion_matrix))
)

validation_summary <- data.frame(
  comments = nrow(validation_comparison),
  agreements = sum(validation_comparison$agreement),
  disagreements = sum(!validation_comparison$agreement),
  agreement_percent = 100 * observed_agreement,
  cohens_kappa = (observed_agreement - expected_agreement) /
    (1 - expected_agreement)
)

print(confusion_matrix)
print(validation_summary, width = 150)

## Save results
dir.create(
  "outputs/youtube/text_analysis",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

write_csv(
  validation_summary,
  "outputs/youtube/text_analysis/validation_summary.csv"
)

  as.data.frame(confusion_matrix),
  "outputs/youtube/text_analysis/validation_confusion_matrix.csv"
)

write_csv(
  validation_comparison,
  "outputs/youtube/text_analysis/validation_comparison.csv"
)

title: Assignment 7: Code and outputs
text:
Aggregate downloads
These are recovered aggregate summaries, not original collection logs or manifests. The quota file is the search plan only. The pre-election summaries show 93 unique relevance results, 97 unique view-count results, and 23 shared videos; earlier channel-count tables still require reconciliation. Validation uses AI-assisted reference labels.
Only existing files are linked below. Place the reviewed CSVs under outputs/assign07/aggregate_tables/ in the website project. The page will render without them but will report missing downloads.
public_files <- c(
  "3a_authors_overall.csv",
  "3a_duplicates_overall.csv",
  "3a_likes_overall.csv",
  "3a_reply_overall.csv",
  "3a_status_by_channel.csv",
  "3a_status_overall.csv",
  "overlap_summary.csv",
  "phrase_counts.csv",
  "quota_plan.csv",
  "search_summary.csv",
  "sentiment_summary.csv",
  "validation_summary.csv"
)
for (filename in public_files) {
  relative_path <- paste0("outputs/assign07/aggregate_tables/", filename)
  if (file.exists(relative_path)) {
    cat("- [", filename, "](", relative_path, ")\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("- Not installed: `", relative_path, "`\n", sep = "")
  }
}
